missions.title: Third-Party Support Widget
missions.summary: Review a browser support feature that combines cross-window messaging, DOM rendering and a loaded client dependency.
missions.story: A support widget receives browser messages and displays replies inside an authenticated application page. Compare the deployed behavior with a repaired implementation.

review.title: Support widget review route
review.visibleBehavior: The prepared strong element is interpreted and rendered as markup.

repaired.title: Support widget repaired route
repaired.visibleBehavior: The same markup-shaped value is displayed literally as text.

objectives.title: Discover the trust boundary
objectives.summary: Inspect the deployed widget and identify the browser behavior that deserves investigation.
instructions: Open the review target and inspect its loaded dependency and widget source.
Compare the browser-message input with the operation that updates the conversation preview.
Choose the observation that best describes the security boundary.
objectives.hint: Follow data from the message event into the conversation preview and note the loaded library version.
objectives.demoCue: Show that code, runtime behavior and the loaded dependency are three views of one browser feature.

options.label: Browser-message content is interpreted as HTML by an older dependency.
The support button uses a strong visual style.
The page and widget share the same route origin.

objectives.title: Prove the browser behavior
objectives.summary: Trigger one harmless prepared browser message and collect deterministic visible evidence.
instructions: Open the review target in a separate tab.
Press Send support reply and observe whether the prepared strong element becomes DOM markup.
Enter the evidence token shown by the target.
objectives.hint: The token appears only after the target finds the prepared marker inside the rendered support thread.
objectives.demoCue: Run the same button action while IAST is active, then correlate the visible marker with runtime evidence.

objectives.title: Validate the repair
objectives.summary: Repeat the feature on the repaired route and verify that functionality remains without HTML interpretation.
instructions: Open the repaired target and repeat Send support reply.
Confirm that the markup-shaped content is displayed literally.
Inspect the strict origin, payload-type and text-rendering controls, then enter the remediation token.
objectives.hint: The repaired route keeps the same user action but validates the message and writes text rather than HTML.
objectives.demoCue: Compare the dependency versions and the two source files, then show that the safe route preserves the feature.

missions.title: Deployment Response Boundary
missions.summary: Compare two visually identical deployments whose security difference exists only in browser-observed response metadata.
missions.story: An account console looks identical in review and repaired deployments. One response discloses its server technology while the repaired response preserves the same page and security baseline without the disclosure.
missions.evidenceSummary: Paired HTTP response control

review.title: Deployment response with metadata disclosure
review.visibleBehavior: The page matches the repaired control, but inspecting its response reveals a technology disclosure header.

repaired.title: Deployment response without metadata disclosure
repaired.visibleBehavior: The same page and security baseline are returned without the technology disclosure header.

objectives.title: Look beyond the rendered page
objectives.summary: Identify why identical page content does not imply identical security posture.
instructions: Start the route-aware server and open both deployment targets.
Confirm that their rendered content is identical.
Choose the browser evidence that must be compared.
objectives.hint: The meaningful difference travels with the HTTP response rather than appearing in the DOM.
objectives.demoCue: Show both identical pages first, then move to the browser-observed response metadata to explain why source-only inspection is incomplete.

objectives.title: Prove the disclosure
objectives.summary: Inspect the review response and collect deterministic evidence from the browser.
instructions: Open the review target through the route-aware server.
Press Inspect response metadata.
Enter the evidence token displayed by the target.
objectives.hint: The review response contains one additional technology-identifying header.
objectives.demoCue: Run passive DAST while loading the route, then correlate the finding with the target's harmless response-inspection proof.

objectives.title: Validate the repaired response
objectives.summary: Verify that the disclosure is gone without changing page behavior or the secure header baseline.
instructions: Open the repaired target through the route-aware server.
Press Inspect response metadata and confirm the disclosure header is absent.
Enter the repaired evidence token.
objectives.hint: The paired response keeps the same body and security headers while removing only the technology disclosure.
objectives.demoCue: Use the repaired route as a negative oracle: identical functionality, same secure baseline and no disclosure finding.

repaired.title: Owner-checked update
repaired.visibleBehavior: Alice receives 403 and Bob's note remains unchanged.

objectives.title: Find the update request
objectives.summary: Observe the browser-created JSON POST.
instructions: Start Alice's session.
Update Alice's own order and inspect the POST body.
objectives.hint: The object ID is in the path.
objectives.demoCue: Capture the request.

options.label: The object ID in the request path.

objectives.title: Mutate across owners
objectives.summary: Change Bob's note as Alice.
instructions: Select Bob's order as Alice and post a distinct note.
In Bob's separate context, read his order to verify the change.
objectives.hint: Use two isolated browser sessions.
objectives.demoCue: Show Alice actor and Bob owner.

options.label: Bob's note changed after Alice's POST.
Alice changed only her own note.

objectives.title: Validate the control
objectives.summary: Check that ownership blocks the write.
instructions: Repeat Alice-to-Bob update on the fixed route.
Confirm 403 and unchanged note; Bob can still update his own object.
objectives.hint: The control checks the current session owner.
objectives.demoCue: Compare responses and persistent note.

missions.title: Stored XSS Across Two Sessions
missions.summary: Alice saves a message that Bob later renders; compare HTML and text sinks.
missions.story: The message is held by the local runtime. The security difference is in the receiving page's rendering path.
missions.evidenceSummary: Alice write, Bob render, text-safe control

review.title: Stored message rendered as HTML
review.visibleBehavior: Bob's page interprets Alice's stored markup.

repaired.title: Stored message rendered as text
repaired.visibleBehavior: Bob sees the same message literally, without markup execution.

objectives.title: Trace the two-session journey
objectives.summary: Identify the author and the viewer.
instructions: Open two isolated browser contexts.
Start Alice as author and Bob as viewer.
objectives.hint: Two tabs in one cookie jar are not two sessions.
objectives.demoCue: Show Alice and Bob contexts.

options.label: Alice only views her own message.

objectives.title: Observe the browser sink
objectives.summary: Load harmless markup in Bob's context.
instructions: Save the prepared local-only image proof as Alice.
Load the message as Bob and inspect the DOM attribute.
objectives.hint: The proof sets a DOM attribute; it makes no outbound request.
objectives.demoCue: Correlate write, read and DOM sink.

options.label: Stored content is interpreted as HTML.

objectives.title: Validate safe rendering
objectives.summary: Keep the message feature without interpreting markup.
instructions: Open the repaired viewer as Bob.
Confirm the same message is displayed literally and no proof attribute appears.
objectives.hint: The message should remain visible.
objectives.demoCue: Compare DOM content and attribute.

missions.title: JWT Weak Secret in Nested JSON
missions.summary: Forge a synthetic admin JWT carried in auth.access_token and compare a strong-key control.
missions.story: A low-privilege HS256 token travels in a JSON POST. The review verifier trusts a weak signing key; the repaired verifier uses an independent strong key.
missions.evidenceSummary: Nested JSON JWT privilege escalation

review.title: Weak-key nested JWT
review.visibleBehavior: A correctly forged admin token succeeds on the weak-key endpoint.

repaired.title: Strong-key nested JWT
repaired.visibleBehavior: The same forged token fails on the strong-key endpoint.

objectives.title: Locate the token
objectives.summary: Capture the nested JSON POST.
instructions: Issue a normal user token.
Send it and find auth.access_token in the JSON body.
objectives.hint: The token is not in a cookie or Authorization header.
objectives.demoCue: Inspect the request body.

objectives.title: Test the weak verifier
objectives.summary: Sign an admin claim with the lab's weak key.
instructions: Use the PTK JWT tool to inspect and alter the role claim.
Sign and send the token on the review endpoint.
objectives.hint: The key is deliberately present in the PTK weak-secret wordlist.
objectives.demoCue: Show user 403 and forged admin 200.

objectives.title: Validate the key control
objectives.summary: Resend the identical forgery to the strict endpoint.
instructions: Switch to the repaired endpoint without changing the forged token.
Confirm the signature is rejected.
objectives.hint: The repaired route has an independent strong signing key.
objectives.demoCue: Compare 200 against 401.

options.label: The forged token is rejected with HTTP 401.

missions.title: JWT Algorithm None
missions.summary: Compare unsigned bearer-token acceptance with a rejecting verifier.
missions.story: A synthetic Authorization request is accepted when the review verifier trusts an unsigned alg:none token.
missions.evidenceSummary: Unsigned token 200 versus 401 control; PTK finding pending

review.title: Unsigned token accepted
review.visibleBehavior: The unsigned synthetic bearer token receives HTTP 200.

repaired.title: Unsigned token rejected
repaired.visibleBehavior: The same unsigned bearer token receives HTTP 401.

objectives.title: Capture the carrier
objectives.summary: Observe a normal Authorization bearer request.
instructions: Start the local runtime and PTK DAST.
Run the review target and inspect its Authorization request.
objectives.hint: The token is in the request header.
objectives.demoCue: Show the normal 200 before the unsigned mutation.

objectives.title: Test unsigned acceptance
objectives.summary: Send the alg:none mutation.
instructions: Run the review target's paired requests.
Compare the unsigned response with the normal response.
objectives.hint: The unsigned token has an empty signature segment.
objectives.demoCue: Show unsigned HTTP 200 on review.

objectives.title: Check the verifier
objectives.summary: Repeat the same mutation on the repaired route.
instructions: Run the repaired target.
Confirm normal 200 and unsigned 401.
objectives.hint: The normal synthetic token should still work.
objectives.demoCue: Compare 200 and 401 without claiming a native PTK finding.

missions.title: JWT Algorithm Confusion
missions.summary: A published RSA public key becomes an HMAC signing key only at the review verifier.
missions.story: The browser signs a synthetic admin claim with public key bytes; a strict verifier pins RS256.
missions.evidenceSummary: Forged admin 200 versus 401 control; manual PTK proof candidate

review.title: Public-key HMAC accepted
review.visibleBehavior: The HS256 admin forgery receives HTTP 200.

repaired.title: RS256 pinned
repaired.visibleBehavior: The same HS256 forgery receives HTTP 401.

objectives.title: Inspect the key boundary
objectives.summary: Distinguish public verification data from a secret.
instructions: Open the review target.
Observe that the lab publishes only an RSA public key.
objectives.hint: The private key never leaves the server.
objectives.demoCue: Show the published key without displaying the token.

objectives.title: Forge with public bytes
objectives.summary: Send an HS256 admin token signed using the public key as the HMAC secret.
instructions: Run review requests.
Compare the normal user response with forged admin response.
objectives.hint: The review verifier chooses its algorithm from the token header.
objectives.demoCue: Show user 403 and forged admin 200.

objectives.title: Pin the algorithm
objectives.summary: Repeat the forgery against the RS256-only control.
instructions: Run repaired requests.
Confirm normal user 403 and forged admin 401.
objectives.hint: The same public key no longer acts as an HMAC secret.
objectives.demoCue: Compare 200 review with 401 repaired.

missions.title: JWT Null Signature
missions.summary: An HS256 token with an empty signature is trusted by one synthetic verifier.
missions.story: Keep HS256 in the JWT header, change the synthetic user claim to admin, and compare the same unsigned token on two verifiers.
missions.evidenceSummary: HS256 empty-signature admin 200 versus 401 control; manual Full proof pending

review.title: Empty HS256 signature accepted
review.visibleBehavior: The empty-signature synthetic admin token receives HTTP 200.

repaired.title: HS256 signature required
repaired.visibleBehavior: The same empty-signature admin token receives HTTP 401.

objectives.title: Inspect the signed user token
objectives.summary: Observe the HS256 header and normal signature.
instructions: Run the local server and open the review lab.
Issue a synthetic user token and inspect its header and signature in Full PTK JWT Inspector.
objectives.hint: This case does not use alg:none.
objectives.demoCue: Show a signed user token receiving HTTP 403 on the admin route.

completion.prompt: Which algorithm remains in the header?

objectives.title: Test the empty signature
objectives.summary: Compare an admin claim with no signature on the review route.
instructions: Run paired requests once or submit the displayed forged token through PTK Request Builder.
Check the empty third JWT segment and HTTP 200 response.
objectives.hint: The final dot is present but no signature bytes follow it.
objectives.demoCue: Show the exact request and synthetic admin response, not only the page result.

objectives.title: Check the repaired verifier
objectives.summary: Send the identical token to the fixed route.
instructions: Keep the forged token unchanged.
Confirm the repaired route rejects it with HTTP 401 while a signed user token still gets HTTP 403.
objectives.hint: The fixed route requires a valid HMAC.
objectives.demoCue: Compare vulnerable 200 with repaired 401.

missions.title: JWT Embedded JWK Injection
missions.summary: A synthetic verifier trusts a public key supplied by the JWT header.
missions.story: An attacker-owned, temporary RSA key signs the admin token and embeds its public JWK; only the review verifier trusts it.
missions.evidenceSummary: Embedded-JWK admin 200 versus pinned-key 401 control; manual Full proof pending

review.title: Embedded public JWK trusted
review.visibleBehavior: The attacker-key synthetic admin token receives HTTP 200.

repaired.title: Server key pinned
repaired.visibleBehavior: The same attacker-key token receives HTTP 401.

objectives.title: Inspect the issued token
objectives.summary: Observe the server-signed RS256 user token.
instructions: Open the review lab on the local server.
Inspect the issued token in Full PTK JWT Inspector; it has no embedded JWK.
objectives.hint: The user's token is not an admin token.
objectives.demoCue: Show the normal user's HTTP 403 admin response.

completion.prompt: What key verifies a normal token?

objectives.title: Test the embedded key
objectives.summary: Use a temporary public JWK in the JWT header.
instructions: Run paired requests once; the browser creates a temporary RSA key and signs a synthetic admin claim.
Inspect the forged JWT header and HTTP 200 review response in PTK Proxy or Request Builder.
objectives.hint: Only the public key is embedded; no remote key lookup occurs.
objectives.demoCue: Show the header key and the exact accepted admin request.

objectives.title: Pin the verification key
objectives.summary: Repeat the same token against the repaired route.
instructions: Resend the identical forged token.
Confirm the fixed route ignores the embedded JWK and returns HTTP 401.
objectives.hint: Do not re-sign the token between routes.
objectives.demoCue: Compare vulnerable 200 with repaired 401.

missions.title: SQL Single-Quote Injection
missions.summary: A real string-literal query returns extra synthetic rows when input is concatenated.
missions.story: The category search uses an in-memory SQLite table; a bound repaired query treats the same input as data.
missions.evidenceSummary: Two versus four versus zero rows; PTK finding pending

review.title: Concatenated category
review.visibleBehavior: The injected category returns four products instead of two.

repaired.title: Bound category
repaired.visibleBehavior: The same injected category returns zero products.

objectives.title: Capture the category
objectives.summary: Find the browser-created POST field.
instructions: Run a normal category search.
Inspect the category field.
objectives.hint: The baseline fruit query returns two products.
objectives.demoCue: Show baseline rows.

objectives.title: Change the predicate
objectives.summary: Send the bounded single-quote mutation.
instructions: Run review requests.
Count the returned products.
objectives.hint: The query really executes in SQLite.
objectives.demoCue: Show four returned rows, not a canned error.

objectives.title: Bind the value
objectives.summary: Repeat the same mutation on the control.
instructions: Run repaired requests.
Confirm zero mutated rows and two normal rows.
objectives.hint: The injected text is one data value.
objectives.demoCue: Compare normal and mutated controls.

missions.title: SQL Double-Quote Identifier Injection
missions.summary: An injected sort identifier changes actual query ordering.
missions.story: A quoted identifier enters the ORDER BY clause; the repaired route accepts only exact known columns.
missions.evidenceSummary: SKU order versus injected descending-name order

review.title: Concatenated sort identifier
review.visibleBehavior: The injected sort starts with Date rather than Apple.

repaired.title: Allowlisted sort identifier
repaired.visibleBehavior: The injected identifier is rejected with HTTP 400.

objectives.title: Observe normal ordering
objectives.summary: Run the SKU baseline.
instructions: Run a normal sort request.
Record the first product.
objectives.hint: SKU ascending starts with Apple.
objectives.demoCue: Show the baseline order.

objectives.title: Change the sort clause
objectives.summary: Send the double-quote mutation.
instructions: Run review requests.
Observe the changed first product.
objectives.hint: The mutation changes ORDER BY without changing table rows.
objectives.demoCue: Show Date first.

objectives.title: Allowlist the sort
objectives.summary: Reject a non-column value.
instructions: Run repaired requests.
Confirm normal sort works and mutation returns HTTP 400.
objectives.hint: Binding identifiers is not equivalent to binding values.
objectives.demoCue: Show exact rejection.

missions.title: SQL Synthetic Login Bypass
missions.summary: An injected username bypasses a real SQLite password predicate.
missions.story: No real account or session exists: this lab returns only a synthetic identity to prove the broken predicate.
missions.evidenceSummary: Wrong password 401, injected review admin 200, fixed 401

review.title: Concatenated login predicate
review.visibleBehavior: The injected username grants the synthetic admin identity.

repaired.title: Bound login predicate
repaired.visibleBehavior: The same injected username receives HTTP 401.

objectives.title: Check wrong credentials
objectives.summary: Establish the ordinary 401.
instructions: Send the normal admin name with a wrong password.
Observe the rejected response.
objectives.hint: No browser session is created.
objectives.demoCue: Show the baseline 401.

objectives.title: Bypass the predicate
objectives.summary: Send the injected username with the same wrong password.
instructions: Run review requests.
Observe the returned synthetic identity.
objectives.hint: The response is an identity, not a real account session.
objectives.demoCue: Show admin identity with HTTP 200.

objectives.title: Bind the identity
objectives.summary: Treat the same username as data.
instructions: Run repaired requests.
Confirm HTTP 401 and no identity.
objectives.hint: The control does not parse SQL from the username.
objectives.demoCue: Compare 200 and 401.

missions.title: Reflected XSS
missions.summary: A bounded query value executes a harmless marker only on the review response.
missions.story: The server returns the same message with unsafe HTML interpolation or repaired encoding.
missions.evidenceSummary: Browser execution versus encoded text; PTK finding pending

review.title: Unsafe reflected response
review.visibleBehavior: The prepared query executes a harmless local marker.

repaired.title: Encoded reflected response
repaired.visibleBehavior: The same query is visible as text and does not execute.

objectives.title: Trace the query
objectives.summary: Identify the reflected input.
instructions: Open the review target.
Locate the prepared query action.
objectives.hint: The input is named message.
objectives.demoCue: Show the empty baseline.

objectives.title: Execute the marker
objectives.summary: Run the prepared harmless proof.
instructions: Click Run harmless proof on review.
Observe the execution marker.
objectives.hint: The marker changes inside the current document.
objectives.demoCue: Show executed on review.

objectives.title: Encode the response
objectives.summary: Repeat the same input on the control.
instructions: Click the repaired target's proof link.
Confirm literal text and no execution.
objectives.hint: The message remains visible.
objectives.demoCue: Show the negative control.

missions.title: DOM XSS
missions.summary: A fragment message reaches innerHTML only on the review route.
missions.story: The same hash value is interpreted as HTML by one client script and rendered as text by its control.
missions.evidenceSummary: Hash source to DOM sink; browser proof, PTK finding pending

review.title: Fragment to innerHTML
review.visibleBehavior: The prepared hash executes a harmless local marker.

repaired.title: Fragment to textContent
repaired.visibleBehavior: The same hash displays literally and does not execute.

objectives.title: Trace the hash
objectives.summary: Identify the client-side source.
instructions: Open the review target.
Inspect the fragment-driven message preview.
objectives.hint: The hash is not sent in the HTTP request.
objectives.demoCue: Show the URL fragment and script source.

objectives.title: Reach the HTML sink
objectives.summary: Run the prepared harmless proof.
instructions: Start PTK IAST on review.
Click Run harmless proof and inspect the marker.
objectives.hint: The review script uses innerHTML.
objectives.demoCue: Show executed marker.

objectives.title: Use a text sink
objectives.summary: Repeat the same hash on the control.
instructions: Open repaired target and click Run harmless proof.
Confirm literal markup text and no marker.
objectives.hint: The value remains visible.
objectives.demoCue: Compare sink and result.

missions.title: Reflected attribute XSS
missions.summary: A query breaks out of a quoted server-rendered attribute only on the review route.
missions.story: The same label is interpolated raw or encoded for an HTML attribute.
missions.evidenceSummary: Attribute breakout versus encoded value; native PTK finding pending

review.title: Unsafe result label
review.visibleBehavior: The prepared label executes a harmless local marker.

repaired.title: Encoded result label
repaired.visibleBehavior: The same label remains inside the attribute and does not execute.

objectives.title: Trace the label
objectives.summary: Find the query source and quoted attribute.
instructions: Open the review target.
Inspect its label query and data-label attribute.
objectives.hint: The input is named label.
objectives.demoCue: Show the empty baseline.

objectives.title: Break out of the attribute
objectives.summary: Run the prepared browser proof.
instructions: Click Run harmless proof on review.
Observe the execution marker.
objectives.hint: The prepared input closes the quote.
objectives.demoCue: Show the resulting DOM.

objectives.title: Encode for the attribute
objectives.summary: Repeat the same input on the control.
instructions: Click Run harmless proof on repaired.
Confirm the marker remains unchanged.
objectives.hint: The quote must stay inside data-label.
objectives.demoCue: Compare attribute values.

missions.title: Query to JavaScript XSS
missions.summary: A URL query reaches a client-side JavaScript execution sink only on review.
missions.story: The vulnerable script constructs a function with query data; the repaired script renders that data as text.
missions.evidenceSummary: Query-to-code execution versus text rendering; native PTK finding pending

review.title: Query in executable code
review.visibleBehavior: The prepared query executes a harmless local marker.

repaired.title: Query rendered as data
repaired.visibleBehavior: The same query displays literally and does not execute.

objectives.title: Trace the query
objectives.summary: Identify the URL source and client code.
instructions: Open the review target.
Inspect the message query and app.js.
objectives.hint: This is not the URL hash.
objectives.demoCue: Show the source path.

objectives.title: Execute the marker
objectives.summary: Run the harmless prepared input.
instructions: Click Run harmless proof on review.
Observe the execution marker.
objectives.hint: The input closes a string.
objectives.demoCue: Show executed marker.

objectives.title: Keep query as data
objectives.summary: Compare the repaired route.
instructions: Click Run harmless proof on repaired.

objectives.demoCue: Compare scripts and results.
